title: Maximal tori in a connected normal subgroup by intersection
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $M\subseteq G$ be a smooth connected closed normal subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Let $T\subseteq G$ be a maximal torus, in the sense of [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]; over $F$ a torus is a group isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some integer $r\geq0$, with $\mathbf G_m$ as in [def-sc-gm-ga]. Form the scheme-theoretic intersection $D=M\times_G T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $D^t=(D_{\mathrm{red}})^\circ$, where reduction is quotient by the nilradical [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] and the superscript denotes the connected component of the identity with its open subscheme structure. Then $D^t$ is a closed subgroup of $D$, is a split torus, and its induced inclusion in $M$ is a maximal torus of $M$. No reductivity of $G$ or $M$ is assumed, and $D$ need not be smooth or reduced. The rank-zero torus is allowed.

source.place: Corollary 17.85, printed pp.379-380; notation 12.29, printed p.241, and Remark 12.5, printed p.232, identify the largest subtorus of a multiplicative group with its reduced identity component over an algebraically closed field.

proof.text: The projection $D=M\times_G T\to T$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. On every $F$-algebra its points are the intersection of two subgroups, so it is a closed subgroup by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. The affine coordinate algebra of $D$ is a quotient of that of $T$; a finite generating set descends, so $D$ is affine of finite type, using [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The same quotient argument applies to $M\subseteq G$. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], $D^0$ is open and closed and $H=(D^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a smooth connected closed subgroup. Reduction has unchanged underlying space and restricts to an open subscheme by quotienting the restricted structure sheaf by its nilradical [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Thus $H=(D_{\mathrm{red}})^0=D^t$. Since $H$ is a smooth connected closed subgroup of the torus $T$, [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus] makes $H$ a torus; over $F$ it is split.

source.place: Corollary 17.85, printed pp.379–380; Theorem 17.10, pp.354–355; Definition 12.14, p.236, and Notation 12.29, p.241. Maximal-containing-torus argument expanded by finite dimension.

proof.text: Every torus $U$ mapping as a closed subgroup into $D$ factors through $H$. Indeed $U$ is smooth by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus], hence reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] applied to $U\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. Pulling a nilpotent function back to a reduced scheme gives zero, so the map factors through $D_{\mathrm{red}}$ by its quotient definition [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Its connected image contains the identity, hence lies in the identity component. Since this component is open, restricting the target gives the factorization through $H$. It remains a closed subgroup inclusion: on affine coordinate rings a surjection factoring through a quotient induces a surjection from that quotient.

source.place: Corollary 17.85, printed pp.379–380; Theorem 17.10, pp.354–355; Definition 12.14, p.236, and Notation 12.29, p.241. Maximal-containing-torus argument expanded by finite dimension.

proof.text: We justify the maximal-torus choices in the source. For $X=M$ or $G$, [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives a finite dimension bound. Every torus $V\subseteq X$ is smooth and connected by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus], and reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] to $V$: since $V=V^0=V_{\mathrm{red}}$, it is integral. It is nonempty because it has an identity. By the chain definition [def-kun-dimension], its dimension is a nonnegative integer at most $\kundim X$: every chain of irreducible closed subsets of a closed subspace is such a chain in $X$.

source.place: Corollary 17.85, printed pp.379–380; Theorem 17.10, pp.354–355; Definition 12.14, p.236, and Notation 12.29, p.241. Maximal-containing-torus argument expanded by finite dimension.

proof.text: Given a torus $A\subseteq X$, choose among torus subgroups containing $A$ one, $V$, of greatest dimension; this nonempty family has dimensions in the finite interval of step 3. If $V\subsetneq W$ for a torus subgroup $W$ of $X$, then $|V|$ is a proper closed subset of $|W|$. To see this, write $V=\operatorname{Spec}(F[W]/J)$ using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. As $F[W]$ is a domain, equality of underlying spaces would force $J$ into the zero prime and hence $J=0$. Since $W$ is irreducible, appending $|W|$ to a longest irreducible closed chain in $|V|$ gives $\kundim W\geq\kundim V+1$ by [def-kun-dimension], a contradiction. Therefore $V$ is a maximal torus of $X$ containing $A$.

source.place: Corollary 17.85, printed pp.379–380; Theorem 17.10, pp.354–355; Definition 12.14, p.236, and Notation 12.29, p.241. Maximal-containing-torus argument expanded by finite dimension.

proof.text: Apply steps 3–4 first to $X=M$ and its identity torus $A=\mathbf G_m^0$ to obtain a maximal torus $S\subseteq M$. The identity is a closed subgroup since $M$ is affine: the evaluation $F[M]\to F$ is surjective. Apply the same argument to $X=G$ and the torus $S\subseteq G$ to obtain a maximal torus $R\subseteq G$ containing $S$. The composite inclusion is closed since the composite of surjective coordinate homomorphisms is surjective [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Corollary 17.85, printed pp.379–380; Theorem 17.10, pp.354–355; Definition 12.14, p.236, and Notation 12.29, p.241. Maximal-containing-torus argument expanded by finite dimension.

proof.text: Both $R$ and the prescribed $T$ are maximal tori of the smooth connected affine finite-type group $G$ over the algebraically closed field $F$. Apply the maximal-torus clause of [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy] to get $g\in G(F)$ with $gRg^{-1}=T$ as subgroup schemes. Conjugation $c_g$ is an automorphism, with inverse $c_{g^{-1}}$, by the group identities [def-sc-group-scheme]. Normality of $M$ gives $c_g(M)=M$ on every commutative $F$-algebra, by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Thus $S_1=c_g(S)$ is a torus subgroup of $M$ and of $T$, hence of their fibre product $D$. It is maximal in $M$: a torus in $M$ containing $S_1$ pulls back under $c_{g^{-1}}$ to a torus containing $S$.

source.place: Corollary 17.85, printed pp.379–380; Theorem 17.10, pp.354–355; Definition 12.14, p.236, and Notation 12.29, p.241. Maximal-containing-torus argument expanded by finite dimension.

proof.text: By step 2, $S_1\subseteq H$. Step 1 makes $H$ itself a torus subgroup of $M$. Maximality of $S_1$ in $M$ therefore gives $S_1=H$. Consequently $D^t=H$ is a closed split torus in $D$ and a maximal torus of $M$. All choices permit the identity torus: if the greatest dimension is zero the same strict-chain argument proves maximality. No smoothness or reducedness of $D$ and no reductivity of either ambient group entered the argument.
